the_measurement_that_stopped_it.what_was_measured: Which lanes this family declares, which of them an interpreter serves, what each of its seven declarations is, and by what route each one's number reaches the coupled walk today. Read live from interpreters.lanes_for, interpreters.INTERPRETERS, interpreters.UNSERVED_LANE_RECEIPTS, item_behavior_catalog.behavior_rules and trigger_stream.CAPABILITIES.
the_measurement_that_stopped_it.the_ruled_act_is_already_performed: umbrella Amendment K rules the retiring act for every one of the fourteen rows to be a per-family interpreter in the family's OWN declared serving lane, and for this row that lane is defense_resolver. INTERPRETERS holds (COMBAT_STATE, DEFENSE_RESOLVER) -- interpreters.combat_state.RESOLVER_INTERPRETER -- so the act this row's retirement consists of has been performed since before the closeout opened, and the committed schedule publishes already_performed: true for it.
the_measurement_that_stopped_it.the_row_stands_on_a_pair_no_ruled_act_re: combat_state declares three lanes (defense_resolver, receipt_walk, compiled_score_walk); INTERPRETERS serves one. scripts/behavior_frontier.py derives counter 4's deferral rows from interpreters.uninterpreted_pairs(), and combat_state/receipt_walk is a member of that tuple. The row therefore retires when and only when that pair leaves it -- which the ruled act, performed in another lane, does not do and cannot do.
the_measurement_that_stopped_it.capability_status_before_the_stop: One of the seven declares a MechanicCapability: force_of_nature.steadfast, engine=walk, authority=COUPLED_AUTHORITATIVE, pairing=SOLO, view_tags={walk: APPLIED}, impl=survival.transitions.update_combat_state. The other six declare none. Authoring the six is half of Ruling 1's shape and is not what stopped the slice -- it is refused here only because it may not land without the other half, which is the whole of Ruling 1's 'either half alone is worse than neither'.
the_measurement_that_stopped_it.how_each_number_reaches_the_walk_today: As resolved defensive state the defense_resolver interpreter granted. The annuls publish a spell shield ready at the opening, the two time stops a stasis the scenario supplied, and Steadfast and Voidborn Resilience publish stack SCHEDULES that carry no resistance at all until the ordered ledger arms them -- which is what force_of_nature.steadfast's own capability names as its walk-side impl, survival.transitions.update_combat_state, reading the fields the resolver wrote. The walk consumes what the resolver built; it does not consume a pair-engine row, and the committed triage measures this family's authored pair rows as none.

why_the_ruled_act_cannot_retire_this_row.the_shape: Amendment L, Ruling 1 rules the retirement act as one behaviour slice carrying, among the rest, 'the lane interpreter landed and wired to the pricing path' and 'the deferral row retired', in one commit. For this row the first half is already true and the second is unreachable from it, because the frontier's deferral row is keyed on (family, receipt_walk) and the ruled interpreter is registered at (family, defense_resolver).

the_three_ways_out_and_why_each_is_refus.register_a_receipt_walk_interpreter: (COMBAT_STATE, RECEIPT_WALK) could be registered. The row's own reason says what that would be -- 'the walks stage what the defence resolver already built, so the declaration reaches them through the resolver interpreter; a walk-lane interpreter here would be a second producer of one number' -- and a second producer of one number is what D-60 and umbrella criterion 8 forbid in terms. Amendment K refuses it in its own words as well: 'It registers no interpreter that emits fields nothing consumes: a counter driven to zero by editing what it counts is worse than the gap.' Measured: all seven declarations are CombatStateRule payloads whose fields the resolver already writes, so a receipt-walk interpreter would emit the same fields from the same declarations and the walk would have two homes for one opening state.
the_three_ways_out_and_why_each_is_refus.drop_the_lane_from_family_lanes: _FAMILY_LANES[COMBAT_STATE] could stop declaring receipt_walk, which is exactly the act Amendment O, Ruling 1 performed for crit_profile. That act is confined by its own words to a family whose declarations all name Subject.HOLDER and which folds only into the holder's own rows, and Amendment O measured this family out of it: combat_state 'declares DefenseField writers with no subject, whose inputs are the subject's live state under combined fire -- a roster input by the authority rule's own list', so 'Ruling 1 closes one row and not six'. Measured again here: all seven payloads carry subject=None, which is the committed triage's declared_subjects of seven 'undeclared'. Editing the table without that ground is the exclusion driven from inside the counter it excuses that D-40 forbids and Amendment K names.
the_three_ways_out_and_why_each_is_refus.call_the_performed_act_the_retirement: The committed schedule answers this in its own words, under what_already_performed_does_not_mean: 'Not that the row retires. INTERPRETERS holding the ruled key is the act being done; the deferral stands because the family still declares a receipt-walk lane the table has no interpreter for, and D-40 forbids editing that table from inside the counter it moves.' A slice that closed the row on that ground would be reading a criterion more weakly than it is written, which umbrella criterion 11 forbids.

why_the_ruled_act_cannot_retire_this_row.why_amendment_p_does_not_reach_it_either: Amendment P is the precedent for a class-(c) row retiring by the ruled act, and it works because damage_routing's row is spelled in the receipt_walk lane: its via is pair_engine, no interpreter of the family serves the lane it declares, and naming a delivery makes a receipt-walk interpreter both possible and consumed. This row is the opposite case. Its via is defense_resolver, its delivery term is ALREADY named and ALREADY standing -- the committed triage publishes walk_side_delivery_term.named: true, where = 'interpreters.INTERPRETERS holds the (combat_state, defense_resolver) key' -- and it is precisely because the delivery stands that a receipt-walk interpreter would be the second producer. Naming a delivery lifts a stop for a row that has none; it cannot lift this one, whose delivery is the reason the row cannot be served.

the_ruled_prerequisite_that_is_missing.what: A ruling naming what retires a (family, RECEIPT_WALK) deferral whose ruled retiring act is performed in a DIFFERENT lane. Two readings are available and each is a decision with a cost: either the three resolver-fed families' receipt-walk lane declaration may be removed from _FAMILY_LANES on the measured ground that the family's delivery is performed in the lane it declares -- an Amendment O, Ruling 1 shaped act on a different ground, with its own machine check and its own reopening condition -- or the rows are closed on some further ground the umbrella names, as Amendment O closed crit_profile's on a ground that was not a retirement at all.
the_ruled_prerequisite_that_is_missing.why_no_lane_may_write_it: Both readings re-scope a debt the umbrella sized. Amendment F sizes the receipt-walk debt and Amendment K settles the lane each row is spelled in while refusing, in three places, to touch _FAMILY_LANES; Amendment O creates the one mechanism that removes a lane declaration and measures this family out of its class in the same paragraph. Choosing between them is a lane deciding what its own criterion means, which umbrella criterion 11 forbids a phase document from doing, and D-40 forbids the edit itself from inside the counter it moves.
the_ruled_prerequisite_that_is_missing.what_it_binds_beyond_this_row: opening_defense/receipt_walk and threshold_defense/receipt_walk are the same shape exactly: the same via, the same already_performed: true, the same _RESOLVER_FED reason and the same class (c) with a named delivery term. Whatever answers this row answers three, which is why the question is worth asking once rather than three times.
the_ruled_prerequisite_that_is_missing.which_row_of_that_ledger_it_is: The NINTH, and the second opened by a retirement lane. Recorded here 2026-08-17 because two of this slice group's commit bodies number it the eighth -- 4ad159b, 'Eighth row of this ledger, and the second opened by a retirement lane', and 6af6689, 'the eighth rulings-owed row opened' -- and an R-35 residue-sweep pass over this group returned the commit-bodies criterion NOT DISCHARGED on exactly that ordinal. A commit body cannot be edited, so the count lands where the row is described. Measured: docs/receipts/rulings-owed.json holds 8 rows at 4ad159b's parent (7 answered, 1 owed) and 9 at 4ad159b, so this slice opened the ninth. The eighth is `whether_a_family_that_authors_no_pair_row_can_retire_off_the_pair_engine`, opened three commits earlier in the same batch by 36e146c, whose body numbers itself 'an eighth row' correctly; and a11bfc9 later numbers its own row the 'Tenth ... and the third opened by a retirement lane', which is only arithmetic if this one is the ninth. The clause the bodies got right is the other one: second opened by a retirement lane, 36e146c's being the first.
the_ruled_prerequisite_that_is_missing.what_the_ordinal_correction_does_not_tou: Nothing else. The sweep pass reports that every other checkable claim in the two bodies verified -- the family's declarations and their subject, the single capability-carrying one, the lane table, the schedule's already_performed flag and the standing receipt_walk rows -- and that the ordinal was the one that did not. Those corroborations are the verifier's measurements and are cited as the verifier's, not re-derived here: this correction is scoped to the claim that was false, and re-stating a verifier's green evidence as though this lane had measured it would be the second-hand number the campaign's own ledger refuses. No number, outcome, population or refusal in this receipt moves, and the row itself is untouched -- rulings-owed.json is a ruled artifact no lane may write.

what_this_receipt_does_not_do: It does not retire the row, re-date it, read the debt as smaller, register an interpreter, or touch _FAMILY_LANES. combat_state/receipt_walk stands in docs/behavior-frontier.json, overdue and gated, with its blocker unchanged; the schedule still sizes it at 2648 leaves across six covering scenarios; and the machine still refuses a row the tree no longer defers. It also does not read the stop as a reason to skip the family's declarations: authoring six MechanicCapability rows on their own would be the counter-moving registration Amendment L, Ruling 1 calls out by name, so they are refused with the rest of the shape rather than banked.

what_this_receipt_owed_next_when_it_was_: One ruling, and then either a retirement slice or a closure act for three rows rather than one. Until it is answered the three resolver-fed rows are the only ones of the nine that cannot be started by the ruled act -- which is a different state from the six that can and that nobody has budgeted, and the difference is worth a reader's time: budget buys those six, and only a ruling buys these three.
the_ruling_that_settled_it: Umbrella Amendment Q, 2026-08-16, and it takes the FIRST of the two branches this receipt's owed ruling offered -- the receipt-walk lane declaration comes out of _FAMILY_LANES on the measured ground that the family's delivery is performed in the lane it declares. The ruling states the ground as a rule rather than as a permission: a family whose walk-side need is satisfied THROUGH its declared serving lane does not need, and must not declare, a RECEIPT_WALK interpreter lane, because one producer is precisely what the one-engine thesis demands -- so a table that goes on asking a second lane for an answer the first lane already gives is asking for the thing criterion 8 forbids, and the deferral row underneath it is counting the absence of a defect. RECEIPT_WALK leaves _FAMILY_LANES for exactly these three measured families, in Amendment O, Ruling 1's shape and on a different ground, and the three rows close as LANE-DECLARATION CORRECTIONS rather than as retirements. What the ruling does NOT do is read Amendment F's fourteen as eleven: three rows leave as mis-declared and say so, which is a correction to a declaration and not a discount on a debt.
the_two_checks_the_ruling_attached_to_th: Both directions, run on every gate run rather than recorded. Forwards, source-asserted per declaration: what each declaration writes is its own resolver interpreter's answer, what consumes it is every read of one of those fields off a resolved defences value in the source outside the resolver, and a declaration nothing consumes fails the gate by name -- which is the ground of this receipt's own how_each_number_reaches_the_walk_today made checkable, including the binding of force_of_nature.steadfast's capability-named impl to a module that is a measured consumer. Backwards: the family's resolver interpreter is removed from the registry the coverage ladder reads, and every declaring owner must then answer withheld naming the missing (family, defense_resolver) pair rather than a modelled status -- a producer whose absence is not a named refusal is the silent zero the campaign exists to invert. The reopening condition is the third clause: a mechanic of one of these families that ever authors walk-priced rows the resolver does not feed puts the lane back and reopens the row.
what_this_receipt_owes_next: Nothing, and the three rows it describes are closed rather than waiting. There is no retirement slice to restart: the ruling settles that a receipt-walk interpreter was never owed here, so the act this receipt refused to force is the act that was never the right one for these families. What remains live is the pair of machine checks: the consumption this receipt described in prose -- the walk consuming what the resolver built -- is now re-derived from source on every gate run, and the day it stops holding, or a mechanic of one of these families authors a walk-priced row the resolver does not feed, the lane re-enters _FAMILY_LANES and this receipt's measurement is what a reader compares against.
what_stands_unedited: Every number, the outcome, the enumerated population of 2648, the three refused ways out and the reason for the stop stand exactly as filed. The answer is recorded BESIDE the question rather than in place of it, which is how rulings-owed.json keeps an answered row's question, measurement and answer joined. `decisions` is not extended either: that list is what the slice landed against, and an amendment dated after the slice stopped is not something it landed against. The one edit to a standing field is its name -- what_this_receipt_owes_next now reads what_this_receipt_owed_next_when_it_was_filed, because a receipt with two answers to one question answers neither.
